purpose: Public facts behind the impact ESTIMATE (scripts/impact_estimate.py). Every fact was read on the page itself on 2026-10-26. Most are career-office ADVICE, not measured averages; the script labels them so. Quotes are under 15 words.

sources.claim: Vanderbilt Owen's Career Management Center tells first-year MBA students to spend 15-25 hours a week on recruiting in the fall, and compares it to an extra class or a part-time job.
sources.quote: students should be spending 15-25 hours weekly towards recruiting
sources.quote_2: Think of it as an additional class or part-time job.
sources.publisher: Vanderbilt University Owen Graduate School of Management (news, Oct 12, 2022)
sources.used_for: sanity check of the weekly total (not an input)

sources.claim: In a RelishCareers survey of business-school students, two-thirds said they spent 4-9 hours a week on recruiting.
sources.quote: two-thirds (66%) spent between 4 and 9 hours on recruiting in an average week
sources.type: self-reported survey, sample size not given, secondary source
sources.used_for: sanity check: what students report doing, as opposed to full coverage

sources.claim: The Carlson School's Year 1 career road map for full-time MBAs says to hold two informational interviews a week in the fall, then two to three a week.
sources.quote: Continue networking and informational interviews two to three per week
sources.publisher: University of Minnesota Carlson School of Management (Career Guide)

sources.claim: Yale SOM's CDO: ask for up to 20-30 minutes; before each informational interview research the company and the contact, prepare questions, practise your story, confirm 24 h before; send a thank-you within 24 hours of every discussion; wait at least a week before following up.
sources.value: 20-30 min per chat; 4 prep steps; thank-you within 24 h; follow-up after >= 1 week
sources.quote: Send a thank you email within 24 hours of every discussion
sources.publisher: Yale School of Management, Career Development Office (2022 guide for working professionals, pp.19-20)
sources.type: advice (working-professionals edition, not the first-year MBA guide)
sources.used_for: chat length (not replaced); the list of per-chat chores (prep, thank-you, follow-up). It gives no minutes for them.

sources.claim: Wharton MBA Career Management tells students to keep a contact-map spreadsheet covering each target company and to follow up 7 business days later if there is no reply.
sources.value: one contact-map spreadsheet covering each target; 3- and 7-business-day follow-up rule
sources.quote: Follow up 7 business days later if no reply
sources.used_for: the follow-up tracking chore exists (minutes are author assumptions)

sources.claim: Steve Dalton's 2-Hour Job Search, in a Chicago Booth CareerCast interview, starts from a list of 40 target employers; on average about 2 of 5 networking emails get a reply.
sources.quote: if you send five emails, you'll hear back from two people on average
sources.publisher: University of Chicago Booth School of Business, CareerCast (Dec 20, 2013)
sources.type: a method's rule of thumb, not a study

sources.claim: Yale SOM's Hiring Organizations 2025-26 page lists the employers where at least one Class of 2025 member took a full-time job or one Class of 2026 member took an internship: 272 names, counted by us from the page's HTML.
sources.value: 272 organisations (full-time and internship employers combined, one year)
sources.quote: one member of the Class of 2026 accepted an internship.
sources.type: official list; total counted by the research agent on 2026-10-26

sources.claim: Yale SOM's CDO page 'Organizations Hiring Yale SOM Students' lists 27 entries under Job Boards (Idealist, Climatejobslist, Biospace, GIIN, ...), including the school's own CMS and several Workmaze guides.
sources.type: official list; count by the research agent
sources.used_for: upper context for BOARDS_USED (a student uses a few of them: author assumption)

sources.claim: Yale SOM's alumni page: more than 13,000 Yale SOM alumni worldwide.
sources.quote: Engage with more than 13,000 Yale SOM alumni worldwide
sources.used_for: size of the alumni search space (context for the people-search minutes)

sources.claim: Yale's fact sheet (2025 data): more than 190,000 living alumni.
sources.quote: 190,000+ living alumni and 296 groups or organizations
sources.used_for: size of the alumni search space (context)

sources.claim: Yale SOM CDO's internship timelines cover 13 industries; networking with alumni, recruiters and employers starts in mid-September, and most industries continue until May.
sources.quote: Mid-September – Begin Conversations with Alumni, Recruiters and Employers
sources.publisher: Yale SOM Career Development Office (file dated 2026/06)

sources.claim: The Yale SOM recruiting calendar set January 30 (2026) as the earliest offer-decision deadline for first-year summer internships.
sources.quote: January 30 | Earliest offer decision deadline for MBA 1Y summer internship roles
sources.publisher: Yale SOM Career Development Office (SOMPost, Jan 2026)
sources.used_for: end of the peak season (SEASON_WEEKS = Sep 15 to Jan 30, about 19.6 weeks)

sources.claim: Vanderbilt Owen's 2026-27 recruiting toolkit sets fall coffee chats at 15-20 minutes.
sources.quote: Schedule 15-20 minute individual or small group (1-3 student) meetings
sources.publisher: Vanderbilt Owen Career Management Center (2026-27 Recruiting Toolkit, employer-facing)
sources.used_for: low end of the chat length (time the app does not replace)

sources.claim: NACE 2024 Student Survey (20,482 college students, mostly undergraduates), asked about obstacles to taking internships: more than 43% said their course load was too high to put the necessary time into the search (the page does not state the denominator).
sources.value: >43% of surveyed college students cite course load
sources.quote: course load was too high to put the necessary time into searching for internships
sources.publisher: National Association of Colleges and Employers (Jan 27, 2025)
sources.used_for: context: time is the binding constraint (not an input)

not_used: McKinsey 'social economy' email-time figure: page not opened, so not cited.
BYU Marriott target-list page: HTTP 403, unverified.
MIT Sloan 'over 270 companies': seen only in a search snippet.
gaps: No career office publishes minutes per task (checking a careers page, finding people at a target, logging a message, preparing a chat, writing a thank-you). Those inputs are author assumptions in the script, each with a low and a high value.
No primary source gives the average number of coffee chats or applications per MBA student; only advised rates (S3, S6).
No school calls recruiting a 'full-time job'; the strongest official wording is 'an additional class or part-time job' (S1).
